items.title: Korea grants temporary stay and work permits to foreign children seeking paternal recognition

items.summary: Foreign children seeking legal recognition from Korean parents can now secure long-term stay rights and legal employment during court proceedings, eliminating a regulatory loophole that often forced vulnerable families into financial hardship or overstaying their visas. Under updated immigration guidelines revealed Friday by the Ministry of Justice, children without citizenship and their custodial parents involved in paternity suits will be eligible for a G-1 visa, a long-term humanitarian status granted in six-month increments for the duration of legal disputes. Crucially, the policy opens a pathway to temporary work permits for parents and guardians following review by an internal human rights committee, allowing them to support themselves legally while navigating the court system. "The measures are designed to fulfill the state's minimum humanitarian obligation by preventing hardship for children of Korean lineage and their guardians during trial proceedings," acting Justice Minister Lee Jin-soo said. The conference had been initially set for Dec. 7 but will take place one week earlier than scheduled on Nov. 30 following a vote by its members. No agenda has been set, but it is expected to include discussions on the judiciary's independence. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) has been pushing for a parliamentary probe into Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, accusing him of interfering in politics. The DPK has accused Cho of meddling in last year's presidential election after the Supreme Court overturned a not-guilty verdict in President Lee Jae Myung's election law violation case and sent it back to a lower court for retrial just ahead of the June 3 presidential election. The university said Wednesday that the new program aims to nurture professionals who can apply AI expertise to the arts and culture sectors. The “AI+Arts Management” program will integrate AI into all aspects of arts management, from performance and exhibition planning to arts organization management, audience development and fundraising. The program will focus on helping students understand how technological advances are transforming the arts and arts management and develop new planning and operational models using AI. Beyond improving work efficiency through AI, the program will emphasize expanding access to arts and culture and generating broader social benefits. It will also support the development of startups that use AI to address social challenges. The curriculum consists of core and elective courses. items.summary: Temperatures in Seoul will drop below zero this weekend as early winter sets in, with strong winds sweeping much of the country Saturday and rain forecast for central regions Sunday. Saturday’s morning lows nationwide will range from minus 5 degrees to 5 degrees Celsius, with daytime highs of 8 to 14 degrees, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration, Friday. Both are below the seasonal norms of 2 to 11 degrees and 13 to 20 degrees, respectively. Cold air moving in from the northwest is expected to bring subzero temperatures, mainly to the central region, eastern North Jeolla Province and inland Gyeongsang areas. The weather agency issued cold alerts for these regions. Seoul's morning lows are forecast to be minus 1 degree, but chilly winds will drive Seoul’s wind chill to around minus 5 degrees. Daytime highes are expected to rise to 9 degrees. Incheon will have temperatures ranging from minus 1 degrees to 8 degrees and Suwon in Gyeonggi Province from minus 1 to 9 degrees. items.title: Korea to see warm, wet winter due to powerful El Nino
items.title_zh: 由于强大的厄尔尼诺现象，韩国将迎来温暖潮湿的冬季
items.summary: Korea is expected to experience a warmer and wetter winter this year due to the influence of a climate phenomenon known as El Nino, the national weather agency said Friday. The Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) said an El Nino — a naturally recurring phenomenon of warming of waters in parts of the tropical Pacific Ocean — has been forming since May and is expected to peak in December. The latest phenomenon is forecast to develop into the strongest on record and bring warm, humid air into Korea this winter, it said, citing record sea surface temperatures of the El Nino monitoring zone. The moving average sea surface temperature for August to October measured 2.4 C above the long-term average, marking the highest for the period since records began in 1950, according to the KMA. Due to the influence of El Nino, Korea's average temperatures in November, December and January are projected to be higher than the long-term averages, with more rainfall than usual in the first two months, it said. items.summary: The veterans ministry said Friday it will invite foreign veterans who fought in the 1950-53 Korean War to the country, along with their family members, to commemorate their service on an annual memorial day. A total of 36 people from six countries and their family members will arrive Sunday for a six-day visit, according to the ministry. The International U.N. Veterans Memorial Day is held annually Nov. 11. The visit is part of the Turn Toward Busan program, which aims to commemorate the service of foreign Korean War veterans. Among the invited veterans is William Walsh, 97, who served as a British Army soldier and trained foreign troops to be deployed to the war at a military battle school, from 1953 to 1955. This year, Canadian veteran Vincent Courtenay, who first proposed the visit program in 2007, along with Kelly McKeague, director of the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency, will also travel to South Korea next week to pay their respects to the U.N. forces, according to the veterans ministry. items.title: Busan shark remains unsighted for 11 days after monthlong stay in canal

items.summary: BUSAN — Bukang-i the shark, which drew more than a million viewers while staying in a coastal canal in the southeastern city of Busan for over a month, has not been seen for 11 consecutive days, raising the possibility that it has finally headed out to the open sea. According to the National Institute of Fisheries Science and relevant agencies, no sightings of Bukang-i have been reported since Oct. 27 near the exit of the canal leading out to Busan's North Port, located about 330 kilometers southeast of Seoul. Experts speculate dropping water temperatures near the canal's exit could have played a role in the shark's disappearance. The optimal water temperature for sharks is between 18 and 26 C, but surface water temperatures off the North Port have fallen to 18-19 C. The shark — affectionately named Bukang-i after Bukhang, Korean for North Port — was first spotted in the canal Sept. 18. items.title: Civil Defense urges caution amid forecast of thunderstorms across Saudi Arabia through Tuesday
items.title_zh: 在周二对沙特阿拉伯各地雷暴的预测中，民防部门敦促谨慎行事
items.summary: RIYADH — The General Directorate of Civil Defense has urged the public to exercise caution and remain in safe locations amid forecasts of thunderstorms hitting across Saudi Arabia from Friday through Tuesday. It called on the people to avoid flood-prone areas and valleys, and refrain from swimming in floodwaters.The Civil Defense cautioned the public to follow instructions issued through various media outlets and social media platforms.The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) reported that the Makkah region is expected to experience moderate to heavy rainfall, potentially causing flash floods, hail, and strong downdrafts that stir up dust and sand. The Riyadh region is also forecast to experience moderate to heavy rainfall, with similar conditions expected in Afif, Al-Dawadmi, Shaqra, Thadiq, Al-Ghat, Al-Zulfi, Al-Majma'ah, Rumah, and Marat. Light to moderate rainfall is expected in Riyadh city, Al-Quwayiyah, Al-Rayn, Dhurma, Al-Hariq, and Al-Kharj.The NCM added that the regions of Jazan, Asir, Al-Baha, Madinah, Hail, Qassim, Al-Jouf, Northern Borders, and Eastern Province are expected to experience moderate to heavy rainfall, potentially accompanied by flash floods, hail, and strong downdrafts that stir up dust and sand.

items.title: Riyadh Metro named among world's top four transport projects
items.title_zh: 利雅得地铁被评为世界四大交通项目之一
items.summary: RIYADH — Riyadh Metro, overseen by the Royal Commission for Riyadh City (RCRC), has been named among the world's top four transport projects at the Smart City Expo World Congress 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. The recognition came amid global competition involving 533 entries from 68 countries, marking a new international achievement that reflects Riyadh's leadership in developing modern and sustainable mobility systems.The ranking recognizes the project's scale and advanced technology as one of the world's largest and most modern public transport projects. Riyadh Metro is a key pillar of a sustainable, environmentally friendly urban transport system that contributes to reducing carbon emissions, improving traffic flow and mobility, and accommodating Riyadh's population growth and rapid urban expansion.During its participation, the commission is showcasing the use of data and modern technologies in city planning and management through the Riyadh Data Hub, digital twin applications, and artificial intelligence. It is also highlighting Riyadh's experience in developing its public transport systemand managing traffic, the Green Riyadh program's efforts, and the capital's major development projects.The congress is one of the leading international gatherings focused on urban development and envisioning the future of cities. This year's edition is held under the theme "Urban Solutions, Real Impact," bringing together more than 600 international speakers to discuss the latest solutions and experiences in digital transformation, mobility, energy, environment, housing, and infrastructure. It also aims to strengthen cooperation to build more efficient and sustainable cities.

items.title: SASO expands proficiency testing accreditation to 65 programs covering 122 technical fields

items.summary: RIYADH — The National Center for Measurement and Calibration at the Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization (SASO) has received expanded accreditation from the Saudi Accreditation Center for its proficiency testing programs, bringing the total to 65 programs covering 122 technical fields.The programs enable measurement and calibration laboratories to assess their technical performance, verify the accuracy of their results, and meet international accreditation requirements. They also strengthen national laboratory capabilities and support Saudi Arabia’s performance in theQuality Infrastructure for Sustainable Development (QI4SD) Index, particularly in laboratory accreditation.The expansion supports sectors including industry, health, food, environment, and trade by improving measurement reliability, product and service quality, and technical efficiency. Laboratories can access the programs through the e-services page on SASO’s website.

items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯拒绝接受《华尔街日报》关于胡塞要求的报道，认为这是“纯粹的捏造”
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Ambassador Dr. Rayed Krimly categorically denied claims published by The Wall Street Journal regarding demands made by the Houthi militia, describing them as “pure fabrication.”In a post on X on Thursday, Krimly rejected the newspaper’s account and questioned the credibility of the information attributed to its sources.“I categorically deny the claims published by The Wall Street Journal regarding demands made by this militia. All of this is pure fabrication by the writers or their alleged sources,” he wrote.Krimly criticized the Houthis for turning against Yemen’s internationally recognized government and contributing to the suffering of the Yemeni people.“These militias turned against the Yemeni government, caused famine among the Yemeni people, and dragged Yemen into conflicts and agendas that do not serve Yemen and its people,” he said.He also condemned the militia’s attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and on civilian and economic targets, as well as its rejection of peace initiatives.“They attacked commercial vessels in the Red Sea waterways, civilian and economic targets, and rejected all peace efforts,” Krimly wrote.The Saudi official concluded by emphasizing the legitimacy of Yemen’s internationally recognized government.“We also remind the writers that Yemen has a recognized government,” he said.

items.title: Pakistan signs Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh
items.title_zh: 巴基斯坦签署2030年利雅得世博会参展合同
items.summary: RIYADH — Pakistan has officially signed its Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh, advancing preparations to develop its pavilion, programs, and experiences for millions of visitors from around the world. The signing reflects the continued momentum of international participation in the event. The Participation Contract was signed by Expo 2030 Riyadh CEO Talal Al-Marri and Pakistani Ambassador to Saudi Arabia and Commissioner General of the Pakistan Pavilion at Expo 2030 Riyadh Ahmad Farooq.Pakistan's participation reflects its deep historical ties with Saudi Arabia and builds on nearly seven decades of involvement in World Expos, demonstrating its continued commitment to the event as a platform for international cooperation and exchange among cultures and peoples.Pakistan's pavilion at Expo 2025 Osaka received a bronze award in recognition of its distinctive design. During the next phase, Pakistan will develop its pavilion in the Culture District at Expo 2030 Riyadh, showcasing its rich heritage, creativity, and aspirations for the future. Speaking on the occasion, Ambassador Farooq said that Pakistan's participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh will provide an excellent platform for showcasing the country's rich legacy in culture, trade, and tourism. “Pakistan holds vast potential and extensive opportunities in trade and investment, while its close ties with Middle Eastern countries, particularly Saudi Arabia, will further strengthen its relations with brotherly countries. We look forward to working closely with the organizers of Expo 2030 Riyadh to ensure successful and impactful participation,” he said.On his part, Al-Marri said: "We welcome the Islamic Republic of Pakistan to the growing list of countries that have officially signed their participation contracts for Expo 2030 Riyadh. This reflects the continued progress of participating countries' preparations as they enter a new phase of developing their pavilions, programs, and visitor experiences for 2030.”Through its pavilion in the Culture District, Al-Marri said, Pakistan will offer an experience combining its rich cultural heritage with its vision for the future. “Given the deep and enduring ties between our two countries, Pakistan's participation holds particular significance. We look forward to working closely with its team and seeing the creative contributions that embody Pakistan's cultural heritage and future aspirations, enriching the global experience Riyadh will host in 2030,” he said.Pakistan's signing of the Participation Contract comes as preparations for Expo 2030 Riyadh accelerate across multiple areas. More than 185 official participants have confirmed their participation, while countries continue developing their pavilions and programs for 2030. Construction is also advancing across the six-million-square-meter site, with infrastructure work progressing and key facilities and assets taking shape.Held under the theme "Foresight for Tomorrow," Expo 2030 Riyadh will provide a global platform for countries to showcase their achievements and ambitions, explore solutions to shared challenges, and open new opportunities for the future. Across its five thematic areas—Technology,Planet, Humanity, Culture, and Collaboration—the event will invite participants and visitors to explore ideas and perspectives that will shape the coming decades.

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Greece sign cybersecurity cooperation memorandum
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯与希腊签署网络安全合作备忘录
items.summary: RIYADH — The National Cybersecurity Authority of Saudi Arabia signed a memorandum of understanding with the National Cybersecurity Authority of the Hellenic Republic to strengthen cooperation in cybersecurity. The signing took place on the sidelines of the fourth meeting of the working group of the Military and Security Committee under the Saudi-Hellenic Strategic Partnership Council. The memorandum is in line with the joint statement issued during Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis's visit to Saudi Arabia on October 25. In the statement, both sides agreed on the importance of strengthening cooperation in cybersecurity and information sharing to protect their core interests and national security. The memorandum also falls within the framework of the committee's work under the council. The memorandum aims to strengthen cooperation between the two countries to protect their cyberspace and vital interests. It covers several areas, most notably the exchange of expertise and best practices to address cybersecurity challenges. The agreement is part of the authority's efforts to reinforce Saudi Arabia's leading international position in cybersecurity, strengthen cooperation and integration with counterpart entities abroad, facilitate the exchange of expertise, and establish mechanisms for cooperation and international partnerships in the field.

items.title: Saudi, Brunei foreign ministers discuss over phone bilateral cooperation
items.title_zh: 沙特，文莱外交部长通过电话讨论双边合作
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan received on Thursday a phone call from Minister of Foreign Affairs of Brunei Darussalam Prince Abdul Mateen. During the call, they reviewed bilateral cooperation between the two countries and ways to further strengthen and develop it. They also discussed issues of mutual interest.

items.title: Crown Prince receives message from Sierra Leone’s president
items.title_zh: 王储收到塞拉利昂总统的来信
items.summary: RIYADH — Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman received a written message from President Julius Maada Bio of Sierra Leone. The message was pertaining to further improving bilateral relations between the two countries. Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Waleed Al-Khereiji received the message for the Crown Prince from Sierra Leone’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Mohammed S. Barrie during their meeting at the ministry’s headquarters in Riyadh on Thursday. During the meeting, they reviewed relations between the two countries and discussed issues of mutual interest.

items.title: Saudi, Iranian FMs discuss efforts to strengthen regional security in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特，伊朗FM讨论努力加强地区安全的电话
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan received on Thursday a phone call from his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi. During the call, they reviewed the latest regional developments. The ministers discussed concerted efforts to strengthen regional security and stability and promote peace and lasting stability across the region.

items.title: Passports Chief inspects Makkah status-correction center to oversee services for Yemenis
items.title_zh: 护照主管视察麦加身份纠正中心，监督为也门人提供的服务
items.summary: MAKKAH — Acting Director General of the General Directorate of Passports Maj. Gen. Dr. Saleh Al-Murabba inspected the status-correction center at the General Services Center in Shumaisi in the Makkah region. The visit aimed to oversee services provided to Yemeni nationals currently in the Kingdom with illegal status who are benefiting from the status-correction initiative. Al-Murabba urged passport staff to intensify their efforts to streamline procedures, enabling Yemeni nationals to regularize their status in accordance with established regulations. He also emphasized the importance of leveraging digital services and ensuring that status-correction centers across the Kingdom are fully equipped to serve the initiative's beneficiaries. It is noteworthy that the General Directorate of Passports started last month procedures to rectify the status of Yemeni nationals residing illegally across Saudi Arabia. This was in line with implementing the directive of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman in response to a request from the President of the Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council Rashad Al-Alimi.
